decisive_items: a well-demarcated, relatively homogeneous mass filling the fourth ventricle
a mildly hypodense, 30 × 40 × 40 mm mass lesion centered in the fourth ventricle region of the posterior fossa
response.rationale: Ependymoma best fits an adult with a well-demarcated, homogeneous fourth-ventricle mass causing obstructive hydrocephalus; the nonenhancing, noncalcified hypodense appearance is less typical of medulloblastoma or choroid plexus papilloma, and the ventricular location is not characteristic of cerebellar astrocytoma.

rejected.why: Medulloblastoma is a key posterior fossa differential, but it is more typically hyperdense and contrast-enhancing and is most common in children; the adult age and nonenhancing homogeneous imaging are less supportive.
Cerebellar astrocytoma usually arises as a cystic cerebellar hemisphere mass with a mural nodule, whereas this mass fills the fourth ventricle and is homogeneous without enhancement.
Choroid plexus papilloma can be intraventricular and cause hydrocephalus, but it is typically lobulated and intensely enhancing; the absence of contrast enhancement is strongly against it.
